h1: Plate bevelling machines — portable cold bevellers for plate and pipe, 1/8″ to 4-3/4″ thick
intro: A plate bevelling machine prepares plate and pipe edges for welding: it sits on the edge, feeds itself along it and cuts the bevel cold — V, X, K or Y, at the angle and depth the weld procedure calls for — so there is no flame cut to clean, no heat-affected zone, no slag and no hours of grinding. NovoTech sells the bevellers of CEVISA, built in Vitoria, Spain, since 1969 and used by boiler and tank makers, structural fabricators, shipyards, wind-tower and offshore builders in more than 60 countries. On this page, small to large: the CHP 7, CHP 12 and CHP 12 INV standard shearing bevellers for plate, tube and discs from 1/8″ to 1-9/16″ thick; the CHP 12G, CHP 21G and CHP 21G INV with the bevel angle adjustable from 20° to 45°; the CHP 12G REV and CHP 21G REV that turn over to bevel the lower edge without turning the plate; and the CHP 30G, CHP 60G, CHP 60G INV and CHP 100G milling bevellers, which machine bevels up to 3-15/16″ wide at 15° to 70° in any material — Hardox, Armox, duplex and stainless included — on plate up to 4-3/4″. Supplied with a CSA-approved panel, installed and supported from Mississauga, ON.

faq.q: What does a plate bevelling machine do?
faq.a: It cuts the bevel a full-penetration weld needs on the edge of a plate or pipe — V, X, K or Y, at a set angle and depth — and feeds itself along the edge while it cuts. Compared with a cutting torch and a grinder it leaves a clean, even bevel with no heat-affected zone, no slag and no scale to grind off, ready to weld, and it does it at several feet a minute with one operator who does not have to hold or guide it.

A shearing beveller (CHP 7 to CHP 21G) takes the bevel off with a resharpenable shear cutter: the fastest and lowest-cost bevel per foot in mild steel, stainless and aluminum, on plate and tube up to 1-15/16″ and bevels up to 1-1/8″. A milling beveller (CHP 30G, 60G, 100G) machines the bevel with a milling head: a machined finish in any material — Hardox, Armox, duplex, super duplex — at the same capacity, angles from 15° to 70°, transition and J bevels, and bevels up to 3-15/16″ wide on plate to 4-3/4″.

Start from the widest bevel face and the thickest plate you prepare. CHP 7: bevels to 3/8″ on 1/8″ – 5/8″ plate and thin tube, also aluminum. CHP 12 / 12G: 11/16″ bevels on 1/4″ to 1-9/16″ (12G 1-3/16″). CHP 21G: 1-1/8″ bevels on 3/8″ – 1-15/16″ plate, for continuous production. CHP 30G: 1-3/8″ machined bevels to 1-15/16″ plate; CHP 60G: 2-3/8″ on plate to 2-3/4″ (3-15/16″ special); CHP 100G: 3-15/16″ on plate to 4-3/4″. In stainless steel the shearing machines take 80 – 90 % of their mild-steel bevel in several runs and about two-thirds in one run; the milling machines keep their full capacity.

faq.q: What do INV and REV mean?
faq.a: An INV (inverted) machine works upside down and bevels the lower edge of the plate, so the lower half of an X or K bevel is cut without turning a heavy plate over; running an INV under its standard twin (CHP 12 + 12 INV, 21G + 21G INV, 60G + 60G INV) cuts both bevels in one pass. A REV (reversible) machine turns over on its frame in under a minute and does both bevels by itself — one machine, one operator.

faq.q: Can it bevel pipe and discs?
faq.a: Yes, the shearing models bevel tube and pipe as well as plate: from Ø3-15/16″ inside (Ø5-7/8″ on the CHP 21G family), on the inside or the outside, with the pipe horizontal or vertical, and discs and tank heads from Ø13-3/4″. The milling bevellers are for plate, flat bar and square bar.

faq.q: What does it cost to run?
faq.a: Little: the shearing cutters last about 3,300 ft (1,000 m) of bevel and are resharpened, Cevisa rates the machines maintenance-free, and a 20 ft plate edge is bevelled in under three minutes on a CHP 12. The milling heads use standard indexable inserts. We quote cutters, inserts and angle devices with the machine.

faq.q: What voltage do these machines run on?
faq.a: Three-phase machines are supplied for 600 V as standard with a CSA-approved panel; 208 V, 240 V and 480 V 3-phase are available on request, and 240 V single-phase on models with a small enough motor. Manual machines have no electrics.
